Changed 'needed an IMF-led rescue' to 'turned to the IMF for a loan', which matches the IMF press release on the Stand-By Arrangement. Reworded the text and added a third EBRD citation (verified on the page): 'Over the last 15 years Hungary has made remarkable progress in transition'.

Thread 'Inflation shock since 2022': removed 'eroding real incomes', which the cited passages do not say. Reworded the causes to match the IMF passage (pandemic, war in Ukraine, crisis-related stimulus).

The OECD 2024 survey is dated March 2024 and the OECD 2026 survey July 2026. The IMF releases are dated 2 August 2024 and 29 August 2025, and the IMF concluding statement 20 June 2025. growth_story.headline: Hungary caught up fast after 1998, stalled after the 2008 crisis, boomed again from 2014, and has barely grown since an inflation shock in 2022.
growth_story.arc: Income per person fell during the break from central planning, at -1.2 percent a year over 1990-1997, with the steepest drop of 11.9 percent in 1991. From 1998 to 2005 it grew 4.4 percent a year, as market reforms, foreign investment and the run-up to EU entry in 2004 lifted output, though budget deficits stayed large. Growth slowed to 0.5 percent a year over 2006-2013: the global financial crisis hit Hungary early and hard, and income per person fell 6.6 percent in 2009. From 2014 to 2025 growth averaged 3.0 percent a year, strong until 2019 and back up to 7.7 in 2021 after the pandemic dip, before an inflation surge in 2022 and blocked EU funds left growth weak: -0.7 in 2023 and 1.0 in each of 2024 and 2025. Over the last decade growth averaged 2.8 percent a year, up from 1.3 in the decade before, and income per person is at its peak in 2025.

threads.title: Transition and EU entry
threads.text: After 1990 Hungary moved from central planning to a market economy, and the EBRD dates most of its gains in competitiveness to 1992-2000. EU entry in May 2004 then lifted output growth and trade.

threads.text: Large budget deficits ran through the early 2000s. When the global financial crisis struck, Hungary was hit early and turned to the IMF for a loan in November 2008; income per person fell 6.6 percent in 2009, and labour productivity began to fall behind that of the G7.

threads.title: Inflation shock since 2022
threads.text: After a quick rebound from the pandemic, growth turned down in the second half of 2022. The pandemic, the war in Ukraine and crisis-era stimulus pushed inflation into double digits, and output has been close to flat since.

since_last_year.text: Growth stayed weak in 2025, with income per person up 1.0 percent, the same as in 2024. The OECD's July 2026 survey found that investment had not begun to recover, but it expected the EU funds blocked since 2022 to be released soon and growth to pick up from 2026.

citations.title: OECD Economic Surveys: Hungary 2026

growth_story.tension: The IMF and OECD describe output as stagnant since 2022, yet the data put income per person at its highest level on record in 2025. The gap is small: after a fall of 0.7 percent in 2023, growth of 1.0 percent in each of 2024 and 2025 only just took income per person past its 2022 level, and income per person can edge up while total output is nearly flat if the population is shrinking.
